https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/msdblad_ec007-1.jpg?&fit=crop&w=1600&h=900
Image via New Line Cinema/courtesy Everett Collection

There have been many Marvel projects that have never seen the light of day, but none of them sting quite as profoundly as the MCU's Blade reboot. When Marvel first announced that Oscar winner Mahershala Ali would be stepping into the role of everyone's favorite vampire-hunting daywalker, there was a huge amount of excitement, especially considering that Blade hasn't gotten his own standalone movie since 2004. Despite having a very small voice cameo in a post-credits scene of Eternals, Ali has made it agonizingly clear that he is done waiting to play the character. MCU fans did get a consolation prize with Wesley Snipes reprising his iconic role in Deadpool & Wolverine, but despite his insistence that "There's only ever gonna be one Blade," one can't help but wonder what could have been with the scrapped reboot.

Perhaps Blade will get his time to shine in the MCU one day, bar his multiversal role in Marvel Zombies, but until then, a new contender to potentially replace Wesley Snipes and Mahershala Ali has thrown his hat into the ring. At a recent Q&A screening of the Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake, hosted by Collider's Perri Nemiroff, series creator Bob Caleb Kane and star William Catlett were in attendance to dish on the behind-the-scenes secrets of the new Linda Cardellini-led show. Catlett is already a horror veteran thanks to the vampire flick Abigail, and it doesn't sound like he's ready to stop fighting the blood-sucking menaces just yet. When asked what was on his "horror moviemaking bucket list," Catlett was reluctant to respond, but eventually admitted he "wouldn't mind" playing Blade, which was met with a hugely positive response from both the crowd in attendance and Kane:
"I worked with Wesley [Snipes]. I don't know why they couldn't make it happen, but that’s something I would like to do."

https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/sharedimages/2024/07/screen-hub-cast-placeholder-1.png?q=49&fit=crop&w=50&h=65&dpr=2

Four powers, and four completely different kinds of person behind them.
Here is what you would wake up with, what it would cost you, and why the MCU keeps handing it to
somebody exactly like you.
Hulk · Marvel Studios · Since 2008
Super Strength

You get the power that is really about taking the hit so that
nobody else has to. Strength in the MCU always lands on people who were already carrying too
much, which is exactly why it suits you.

Your instinct is to put yourself between the problem and the people, and you do it
before anybody has thought to ask.

Bruce Banner is the most interesting version of this because his story was never about
lifting things, it was about control.

The catch with strength is that people stop checking whether you are alright, since you
have made a habit of looking like you always are.

You would be the one everybody calls at two in the morning, and you would answer every
single time.
Spider-Man · Marvel Studios · Since 2016
Spider-Sense

You get the power that never switches off. Spider-sense is a gift
and a nervous system on permanent alert, and the people who get it in these films are always
the ones who were already worrying about everybody.

You read a situation faster than you can explain it, and you are usually right in a way
you cannot show your working for.

Peter Parker is the template because he takes on more than he can hold and then
apologises for not holding it well enough.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day arrived in July 2026 and put him back to being local, broke
and permanently on call.

The cost here is real, since a power that warns you about everything also means you are
never quite off duty.
The Fantastic Four · Marvel Studios · 2025
Invisibility

You get the quietest power in the building, and quietly the most
useful. Invisibility comes with force fields for a reason, because the people who prefer not
to be seen are usually the ones holding a shield around everybody else.

You notice everything, largely because you spend more time observing a room than
performing in it.

Sue Storm is the strongest member of her team and the least interested in anybody saying
so, which is very much your energy.

The Fantastic Four: First Steps finally gave the family a proper MCU home in 2025 and
made her the centre of it.

Your risk is that being unseen becomes a habit rather than a choice, and the people who
love you would like a look in.
Scarlet Witch · Marvel Studios · Since 2015
Chaos Magic

You get the biggest and least comfortable power on the list, the
one that runs directly on feeling. Chaos magic is not really a superpower in the MCU so much
as an emotional state with consequences attached.

You feel things at a volume other people do not, and you have spent years managing that
rather than being managed by it.

Wanda is the best written character Marvel has, precisely because her power and her
grief turned out to be the same thing.

WandaVision remains the high point of Marvel television, and it works because the
spectacle is only ever a symptom.

The warning attached to this one is simple. A power that answers to how you feel is only
ever as steady as you are.
↻ RETAKE THE QUIZ
'Crystal Lake' Delivers a Dramatic New Take on the Voorhees Family's Origin Story

Hopefully Catlett's dream of playing Blade comes true, but until then, he faces a totally different kind of threat as the sheriff of a small notorious town known as Crystal Lake in Peacock's new original series. Taking place years before the events of the original 1980 film, Crystal Lake sees Linda Cardellini as a young Pamela Voorhees as she tries to cope with the disappearance and presumed death of her son Jason (Callum Vinson). It's a bold creative shift for the franchise that focuses on the horror saga's most notorious villains rather than its victims, and it's bound to craft a fascinating origin story for everyone's favorite machete-wielding family of serial killers.
Crystal Lake premieres exclusively on Peacock on October 15. Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.
